notes: Shopify store, HTTP fetch (curl) tier-1 only, no bot protection, no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow. Home-page mega-nav has a top-level 'Sale' menu (data-url /collections/shop-all-sale) whose children are: 'Shop All Sales' (shop-all-sale, 1009 products), department pages 'Furniture Sale', 'Curtains & Blinds Sale', 'Decor & Pillows Sale', 'Wall Decor & Mirrors Sale', 'Junior Sale', 'Lighting Sale', 'Bed & Bath Sale' (all generic, no permanence/outlet language, excluded as temporary promotional Sale per brief's Sale-vs-Clearance test), AND one item literally labeled 'Clearance' pointing to /collections/markdowns. This is the site's own taxonomy signal (nav label text = 'Clearance', page H1/title = 'Clearance') so /collections/markdowns is recorded as the Clearance row -- 177 unique product IDs via exhaustion-paged products.json. Also found /collections/20-off-clearance via sitemap (not in main nav, title '20% off Clearance'); compared product-ID sets and it is a 100% overlap alias of markdowns (177/177 identical IDs) -- same underlying listing, so NOT recorded as a separate row; canonical URL kept is /collections/markdowns (the nav-labeled 'Clearance' page). Checked /collections/selling-fast (310 products, H1 'Deals selling fast'): 0/310 overlap with markdowns' product-ID set, so it is not part of Clearance (it overlaps 215/310 with the generic Sale hub instead) -- excluded, not flagged ambiguous, since the non-overlap with Clearance and overlap with generic Sale gives a confident answer rather than a genuine toss-up. Discovery method: sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml (375 handles) grepped for clearance/outlet/final-sale/last-chance/end-of-line/markdown/solde/liquidation, plus full home-page nav HTML parse. Did not use site search (robots.txt disallows /search; nav+sitemap fully covered discovery).
